items.item_text: Meet with senior leadership to help guide and prioritize DSI projects and resourcing.
Provide project management by coordinating timelines, tracking progress, and ensuring stakeholders remain informed throughout the project lifecycle.
Establishes standards for system ownership, data stewardship, process documentation, and operational readiness before implementation.
Define project scope, decision rights, milestones, dependencies, risk levels, and accountability structures in partnership with functional owners.
Ensure each project has identified sponsors, business owners, data owners, technical owners, deadlines, and success measures.
Hold project participants accountable for deliverables, decisions, testing, documentation, and timely communication.
Identify stalled, under-resourced, duplicative, or misaligned projects and recommend corrective action to the VP and senior leadership.
Conduct post-implementation reviews to ensure plan objectives are met, evaluating successes, identifying areas for improvement, and recommending additional process enhancements.
Collaborate with functional users and technical teams to identify challenges, develop solutions, and communicate system updates in ways that are accessible and actionable for the campus community.
Lead change management planning for system, data, and process changes that affect campus operations.
Develop communication, training, adoption, and transition plans to support successful implementation.
Ensure functional users understand new processes, deadlines, responsibilities, and consequences of non-adoption.
Partner with departments to identify workflow impacts and ensure operational readiness before launch.

Guide the Data Management & Integrity Committee in partnership with all data stewards to develop intentional and comprehensive policies and practices for using and leveraging institutional data as the co-chair.
Operationalize the institutional standards for data definitions, data quality, system documentation, access protocols, reporting logic, and data stewardship.
Coordinate with data stewards to resolve conflicting definitions, inconsistent business practices, and data quality issues.
Serve in the Enrollment management working group as the DSI co-chair to support Strategic enrollment management initiatives.
Oversee the maintenance of institutional data dictionary and data democratization for the institution in partnership with all data stewards.
Foster a data-informed decision-making culture across campus through collaboration, communication, and effective use of reporting and system solutions.
In partnership with the VP, set the annual goals for DSI.
Partner with Information Technology and Finance to ensure maximum utilization of software inventory, coordination between systems, and deduplication of efforts.
Vendor review and management oversight for supported applications.
A growth mindset.
A passion for people and values them over processes and tools.
A collaborator with a focus on providing solutions based on the requirements and necessary outcomes of those whom we serve.
The aptitude for responding to change over following a set plan.
Ability to gather user requirements and help develop solutions.
Ability to instruct others, both individually and in a group setting.
Ability to interact productively and collaboratively with a diverse campus population.
Ability to prioritize, plan work activities to use time efficiently while satisfying deadlines and expectations.
Provide high-quality customer service.
Speak and write English clearly and persuasively with attention to detail and the needs of the target audience.
Staff
*Must have access to reliable and secure computer and internet connection.

*Must have access to a dedicated and suitable workstation at remote location, including desk or table and supporting, upright chair. Must ensure workstation is safe and free from hazards and ergonomically appropriate.
